subject: EdgeFin: Performance/SLO benchmark methodology follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@edgefin.com>, Samantha Li <samantha.li@edgefin.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2027 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + next steps: perf / SLO qualification + benchmark methodology

Thanks again for the call earlier, Carlos and Samantha — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on performance and SLO requirements for the PoC: 

- Business SLOs you called out:
  - 95th percentile latency goal for user-facing generation: <= 300ms for prompt lengths up to 128 tokens (streaming enabled).
  - Sustained throughput target: 200 concurrent requests at ~1k tokens/sec aggregate (burst to 500).
  - Streaming requirements: token-by-token streaming with first-token latency <= 120ms, and stable token emission thereafter.
  - Cold-start and warm-cache behavior matters: you want numbers for both.

- Benchmark methodology items we agreed to exchange:
  - Prompt set (representative user prompts + edge cases).
  - Eval harness (how you measure latency, concurrency load pattern, and streaming token timings).
  - Definition of metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 for both first-token and end-to-end, throughput (tokens/sec), and error rates under load.
  - Reproducibility notes (seeded randomness, model/version pinned, hardware profile).

Requested next steps: 
1) Carlos to share the prompt set (JSONL) and any golden outputs / eval criteria by EOD Wednesday.
2) Redwood to provide a recommended benchmark harness (how we run tests, tooling we use) and a short runbook for reproducibility.
3) Engineering sanity-check: Rishi / dev team to confirm whether the targets above map to an achievable config and propose a test window.

Attachments: edgefin_benchmark_requirements.pdf (high-level SLO doc).

If that matches your notes, we'll set up a 30-min alignment call after you share the prompt set.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

From: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Li <samantha.li@edgefin.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2027 17:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: perf / SLO qualification + benchmark methodology

Thanks Marissa — great summary and yes, that matches our internal notes. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- The 300ms p95 is for the live web UI (single-turn completions) with streaming enabled; for background batch jobs the throughput requirement is more important than latency.
- For streaming, first-token under 120ms is ideal but we can be flexible to 150ms if overall token churn is stable.
- Cold-start: we measure cold as >30 minutes idle on the model instance. Warm is sustained traffic for >5 minutes.

I'll share the following by EOD Wednesday: prompt_set_v1.jsonl (representative prompts), a small golden set (20 examples) with expected safety/formatting checks, and a doc describing how our own harness currently measures token latency.

Quick ask: can Redwood provide an isolated test account or temporary API key with a pinned model version & instance profile so we can run the same harness reproducibly? Also include the exact hardware profile you plan to use for the benchmark (GPU type, memory, region).

Attachments: prompt_set_v1.jsonl (will be attached in next mail), eval_harness_readme.md (will follow).

Best,

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2027 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Recap + next steps: perf / SLO qualification + benchmark methodology

Thanks Marissa — taking this on. Quick technical reads and asks so we can prepare a reproducible harness: 

1) Measurement definitions (we'll standardize these in the harness):
   - first-token-latency: server time from request recv -> first token sent (ms).
   - end-to-end latency: server time from request recv -> last token completed (ms).
   - token-rate: tokens emitted per second per instance.
   - concurrency: number of simultaneous active requests.
   - error-rate: 4xx/5xx/timeout counts per run.
   - p50/p90/p95/p99 for both first-token and end-to-end latencies.

2) Baseline config we will test initially:
   - Model: open-llama-13b (pinned sha), quantized FP16 where supported.
   - Instance: 1x A100-80GB (or equivalent). We'll also run a 2x A100 parallel config if single instance can't meet concurrency.
   - Serving knobs: batch size tuned for 128-token prompts (auto-batching on with 50ms max batch delay), KV cache warmed for warm run.
   - Streaming API: chunk size 1 token, flush immediately.

3) Reproducibility/runbook requests for EdgeFin to provide in their prompt set doc:
   - JSONL with explicit metadata: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_max_tokens, seed (if stochastic), and any postprocessing expected.
   - A golden set for functional checks (they mentioned 20 examples).
   - Their harness should include the exact concurrency pattern (ramp, sustain, burst) they ran earlier.

4) Proposed schedule:
   - Dry run (sanity): Monday 2027-02-15 09:00-11:00 PT (internal only).
   - Customer-run benchmark: Tuesday 2027-02-16 13:00-15:00 PT (invite EdgeFin).

5) Test account / API key: We can provision a scoped test API key for EdgeFin pointing to a dedicated instance with pinned model/version. I'll coordinate with infra to provision and provide hardware details (A100-80GB, region us-west1) in the runbook.

I'll prepare a small repo with the harness (README + runner) and share the Drive link once ready. Planning to include automated metric export (CSV + JSON) and instructions to seed randomness and pin model.

If this looks good I'll: (a) create the harness repo, (b) provision test credentials, (c) schedule the runs in calendar and share invites.

—Dev Patel
